title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description:
Imagine standing on the right side of a binary tree. Report the values of the nodes you can see, ordered from the top level to the bottom. At each level you see the right-most node.

Input format
One line: the tree in level-order, values separated by spaces, with the word null for a missing child. Children of null nodes are not listed (the usual level-order serialisation). For example "3 9 20 null null 15 7".

Output format
The visible values on one line separated by single spaces, or the word EMPTY for an empty tree.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes <= 100000. Values are integers.
hints: How many nodes can you see at each depth of the tree?
Do a level-by-level (breadth-first) traversal; the last node of each level is the one you see.
A node deeper in the left sub-tree can still be visible when the right sub-tree is shorter. Do not simply follow right children.

examples.explanation: Level 1: 1, level 2: 3 is right-most, level 3: 4 is right-most.
Only left children exist, so the left nodes are what you see.
